themes_detail.label: Graffiti surge this week
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints spiked to 5 THIS WEEK compared to a 0.5 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 900% increase (z-score: 6.36)—suggesting either a coordinated tagging campaign or enforcement gap in Queens Village/Cambria Heights.
evidence: 5 graffiti complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (900% spike, z-score 6.36)
Spike is brand new and concentrated in a single week, not a gradual trend
High statistical significance indicates this is not random variation
reporting_angles: Map complaint locations to identify whether graffiti is clustered in specific neighborhoods or corridors
Interview NYPD and Parks enforcement about whether they've detected any organized tagging groups or recent vandalism patterns

themes_detail.label: Vehicle noise complaints triple
themes_detail.summary: Vehicle noise complaints jumped to 15 THIS WEEK versus a 4.5 weekly average over 8 weeks—a 233% surge (z-score: 6.06)—pointing to a possible surge in illegal street racing, modified exhausts, or loud vehicle gatherings in the district.
evidence: 15 noise-vehicle complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (233% spike, z-score 6.06)
This is a fresh signal appearing this week, not a lingering issue
High z-score (6.06) indicates statistically significant deviation from baseline
reporting_angles: Canvas residents near hotspot complaint locations to document the nature and timing of vehicle noise incidents
Interview NYPD about enforcement activity targeting illegal street racing or modified vehicles in Queens Village

themes_detail.label: Tree and landscape emergency
themes_detail.summary: Over the past 3 weeks, overgrown tree/branch complaints (37 three weeks ago vs. 10.6 weekly average, +248%) and new tree requests (3 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 average, +700%) have spiked together, alongside uprooted stump reports—suggesting weather damage, deferred maintenance, or a tree-planting/removal backlog affecting the district.
evidence: New Tree Requests: 3 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average (700% spike, z-score 5.42)
Overgrown Tree/Branches: 37 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 10.6 weekly average (248% spike, z-score 5.3)
Uprooted Stump complaints: 3 three weeks ago vs. 0.5 weekly average (500% spike, z-score 5.0)
Convergence with recurring community board budget requests for 'better park maintenance' and park reconstruction (cited [01] times)
reporting_angles: Request data from Parks Department on tree maintenance backlog, recent storm damage, and timeline for addressing overgrown branches endangering sidewalks
Interview residents about sidewalk blockages and safety hazards from overgrown vegetation; investigate whether emergency tree removal requests are being prioritized

themes_detail.label: Curb and street deterioration spike
themes_detail.summary: Curb condition complaints surged to 15 three weeks ago versus a 2.2 weekly average—a 567% spike (z-score: 8.17)—indicating rapid pavement failure that may endanger pedestrians and cyclists, particularly given concurrent street condition complaints (2,546 over 90 days).
evidence: Curb Condition: 15 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 2.2 weekly average (567% spike, z-score 8.17, highest statistical significance in dataset)
Street Condition is the top complaint category overall (2,546 complaints over 90 days)
Convergence with recurring community board budget request for 'Reconstruct streets' (cited [01] times, year-over-year unsolved)
reporting_angles: Obtain DOT street inspection data and prioritization queue for Queens Village; compare complaint hotspots with actual repair schedules
Photograph worst curb/street damage and interview residents about accessibility issues for elderly, disabled, and families with strollers

themes_detail.label: Illegal parking enforcement gap widening
themes_detail.summary: Illegal parking complaints climbed to 205 TWO WEEKS AGO versus a 153.0 weekly average—a 34% increase (z-score: 3.43)—suggesting either declining enforcement or a parking shortage driving residents to curb violations.
evidence: Illegal Parking: 205 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 153.0 weekly average (34% spike, z-score 3.43)
Illegal Parking is second-highest complaint type overall (2,045 over 90 days), with this recent spike on top of chronic problem
Convergence with recurring community board requests for enforcement expansion (cited [01] times)
reporting_angles: Interview NYPD Parking Enforcement about staffing, ticket issuance trends, and whether tickets have dropped recently
Survey residents and local merchants about parking availability and whether illegal parking is blocking driveways or creating traffic hazards
